Translation goal: reverse-translatability for the Tafsir reader — readers should be able to map English back to JA. Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And these are the blessings with which Moses, the messenger of God, blessed the sons of Israel before his death.
translations.2: And he said: O God, who revealed Himself to us from Mount Sinai, and shone with His light from Mount Seir, and flashed with it from Mount Paran, and came to the myriads of the holy ones — with His laws, a light from His right hand, for them.
translations.3: And He also cherished a people for Himself; so all their choicest ones are in obedience to You, and they follow in Your footsteps, and pass on Your words one to another.
translations.4: O God, who commanded us through Moses with the Torah — and made it an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob.
translations.5: And there was a king among the described one, when his chiefs and the rest of his tribes would gather to him.
translations.6: I ask of You that the clan of Reuben live and not die, and not become a group too few to count.
translations.7: And this is what he said for Judah: O God, hear the voice of Judah, and return him to his people from his campaign; and make his two hands prevailing for him, and be for him a helper against his enemies.
translations.8: And he said for Levi: O God, who granted Your Thummim and Your Urim to a man who is Your devoted one — and You tested him at the very trial, and contended with him at the water of contention.
translations.9: And You found him to be one who says of his father and his mother, as though he had not seen them; and did not acknowledge his brothers, and did not recognize his sons — because they guarded Your word, and they keep Your covenant.
translations.10: And so they give rulings in Your laws for Jacob, and Your statutes for Israel; they set the incense before You, and the whole-offering upon Your altar.
translations.11: O God, so bless his host, and be pleased with what his two hands do; and weaken the loins of those who oppose him and hate him, so that they cannot stand against him.
translations.12: And he said for Benjamin: Since he is the beloved of God, he shall dwell in confidence in Him; and He shall compass him all the length of time, and between His heights He shall dwell.
translations.13: And he said for Joseph: O God, so bless his land — with the delights of Your heavens and their dew, and with the deep waters crouching beneath.
translations.14: And with the delights of the produce of the sun, and the delights of the grain of the moon.
translations.15: And with the ancient roots of the mountains, and the perennial branches of the heights.
translations.16: And with the bounty of the earth in full, and the favor of the One who dwells in the thornbush — may all this come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the one set apart from his brothers.
translations.17: And let the glory belong to the one likened to the firstborn of his ox; and his horns shall be as the horns of the wild ox, so that with them he shall gore the nations to the ends of the earth — and the explanation thereof is that they are the myriads of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh.
translations.18: And he said for Zebulun: Rejoice, O Zebulun, in your journeys; and you, O Issachar, in your dwellings.
translations.19: For the nations shall come of their own accord to your mountain, and shall offer righteous sacrifices there; for they shall suck the abundance of the seas, and they shall treasure the hidden things of the sand.
translations.21: And he saw, in the foremost part of his land, that the congregation of those who traced it was stored there; so he came to the chiefs of the people and made them disciples — and he acted according to the justice of God and His laws, together with the rest of the clan of Israel.
translations.22: And he said for Dan: Be, O Dan, like the cub of a lion in strength, as it springs forth from the Bashan.
translations.23: And he said for Naphtali: O Naphtali, gain much of favor, and be filled with the blessings of God; and possess from the land westward and southward.
translations.24: And he said for Asher: Be blessed of the saints, O Asher, who shall be the delight of his brothers, and who dips his foot in oil.
translations.25: Your bolts shall be of iron and bronze, and as your days are, so shall your strength be.
translations.26: The God of Israel, who has no likeness — the Dweller of the heavens and the heights, in His power, is your help.
translations.27: And He is the abode — the God eternal — and beneath Him are the kings of the world; even as He drove out the enemy from before you, and said to you: Destroy him.
translations.28: Until some of the clan of Israel settled in confidence, each apart, in fulfilment of what Jacob their father told them — in a land of grain and wine-press; and moreover its sky pours down dew.
translations.29: So blessed are you, O clan of Israel — who is like you? A people succored by God; and He is your shield and your help, and your sword and your might. So shall your enemies submit to you, and you shall tread upon their heights.
